title: 70% of Japanese Kids Read Less than an Hour a Week
paragraphs: Many children in Japan like books, but they do not spend much time reading them, according to a new survey.

The survey was done by the Hakuhodo Foundation, a Japanese organization that studies children and education. In August 2026, it asked 1,200 children from the fourth grade of elementary school to the third year of junior high school about reading.

The survey found that 72.6% of children read for less than one hour a week. This includes 17.4% who do not read at all and 55.2% who read for less than an hour. Junior high school students read less than elementary school students. About 22% of junior high school students said they do not read at all.
However, many children still like reading. About 69.3% said they like to read books. But 76.5% said that videos and games are more fun than books.
The most popular kinds of books were novels and stories, followed by manga. Many children find new books at their school library or at bookstores.

Parents seem to make a big difference. In families where parents read for more than one hour a week, 91.8% of children said they like reading. Parents of children who love reading often choose books for them, read to them, and take them to libraries and bookstores.
Schools also help. About 65.5% of children borrowed books from their school library in the past year.
